page.overview:
Who is Alamosaurus?

(meaning "Ojo Alamo lizard") was an American titanosaur, found in Texas and named after Ojo Alamo - a formation in Texas where it was first discovered. It was the last and largest sauropod known from North America and may well have been prey to Tyrannosaurus. The name Alamosaurus means "lizard from the Alamo". One of the last sauropod dinosaurs, the largest individual is about 26 meters long and weighs 38 tons, rivaling the size of other titanic sauropods such as Argentinosaurus.

A skeleton of Alamosaurus stood in what was once the Visitor Center of the original Jurassic Park, along with a neighboring Tyrannosaurus rex skeleton. Alan, Ellie, Lex, and Tim attempted to use it to climb down from the ceiling to escape a member of the Velociraptor pack, whose attack caused the skeleton to fall apart.

Alamosaurus was referred on the inactive species list of Isla Adventura. However, it is revealed that a population of Alamosaurus have existed on Isla Sorna.

When the Visitor Center appears in other Jurassic Park media, Alamosaurus is often replaced by diplodocid sauropods such as Apatosaurus (LEGO Jurassic World) or Brontosaurus (Jurassic Park Discovery Center).
